content: Question posed: does catalytic inhibition of HDAC5 reproduce protein reduction on SLC2A1/GLUT1 in human neural cells; compare catalytic, scaffold, localization; paralogs separate; beneficial/compensatory/harmful in WWOX deficiency; deciding experiment
note: framing; repeated twice; L2-3 contain UI text 'View full report'

content: Disorder stated as WWOX-related DEE (WOREE syndrome; MONDO:0014533)
Headline answer: No; catalytic inhibition is not expected to reproduce protein reduction for SLC2A1/GLUT1
HDAC5 is a class IIa 'pseudo-enzyme'; its repression of MEF2-driven genes (pathway governing SLC2A1/GLUT1) is deacetylase-independent
note: MEF2 governs SLC2A1 asserted without citation

content: Scaffold function: nanomolar sequestration of MEF2 plus recruitment of catalytically active NCoR/SMRT-HDAC3 complex
note: HDAC3 recruitment claim carries no reference

content: Localization function: signal-regulated nucleocytoplasmic shuttling determines nuclear residence and repression
Knockdown/degradation removes all three functions (weak catalysis, scaffold, localization); catalytic-site inhibitor removes only the first and weakest; the three are pharmacologically non-equivalent
Predicted divergence lies at the scaffold/MEF2 arm that controls GLUT1
GLUT1 change is most plausibly compensatory/beneficial in WWOX deficiency (fuel delivery against energy/glucose starvation)
note: labelled weighted inference, moderate confidence (L45, L112)

content: Wwox-null mice die early of hypoglycemia and metabolic failure (death by 3-4 weeks); quoted as 'develop normally in utero but succumb to hypoglycemia'
Neuronal WWOX restoration rescued hyperexcitability, seizures, hypoglycemia, myelination deficits, lethality and behaviour in Wwox-null mice; curated in WWOX-DEE knowledge base
note: also attributed to knowledge base; report ties disorder to rescuable glucose-supply deficit (inference)

content: In GLUT1-deficiency syndrome mutants, augmenting GLUT1 raised CSF glucose, improved motor performance and reduced seizure frequency
Pre-/early-symptomatic AAV9-mediated Glut1 repletion averts brain microvasculature defects and prevents disease
A GLUT1 increase opposes the WWOX energy deficit and parallels an established therapeutic direction (analogy to GLUT1DS)
Cancer-context: WWOX loss drives GLUT1 up via HIF1alpha-dependent aerobic glycolysis (maladaptive Warburg shift)
note: named principal formal alternative; report says not formally excluded in neurons; 27308416 is a commentary naming HIF1alpha, not GLUT1; the 'WWOX loss raises GLUT1' reading is the report's

content: Alternative coexists with beneficial reading; which axis dominates in post-mitotic hypoglycemic neurons is open; direction is a weighted inference needing functional confirmation
WWOX 'modulates HIF1alpha, thereby regulating' aerobic glycolysis; HIF1alpha drives glycolytic gene program including SLC2A1
note: HIF1a-SLC2A1 step stated without separate citation; 27308416 is a short commentary whose abstract names HIF1alpha but not GLUT1/SLC2A1

content: WWOX-DEE knowledge base entry: WWOX is a loss-of-function scaffold hub with no known catalytic substrate; seizure phenotype driven by GSK-3beta hyperactivation; lithium abolishes PTZ seizures in Wwox-/- mice
note: internal KB, not a literature source

content: Because WWOX deficiency already raises GLUT1-related uptake via HIF1alpha, direction of any further HDAC5-driven GLUT1 rise is a priori ambiguous (compensatory vs deeper Warburg)
note: tension with starvation framing at L39

content: SLC2A1 haploinsufficiency causes GLUT1-deficiency epileptic encephalopathy; ketogenic dietary therapies provide ketones as alternative fuel and control seizures
note: report infers higher glucose-transport capacity is generally protective; ketone benefit is alternative fuel, not GLUT1 rise

content: Higher brain glucose-transport capacity is generally protective against seizures
In myocardial infarction model, exercise activated AMPK, which phosphorylated HDAC4 and raised GLUT1 by relieving HDAC4 inhibition of MEF2a
note: cardiac, HDAC4; direct quote about 35 words in report

content: Relief of HDAC4 inhibition came from phosphorylation and mislocalization, not from blocking catalysis
note: gloss by report, not the abstract's statement

content: HDAC4 represses the beta-catenin to GLUT1 program (TUG1/miR-340/HDAC4 axis); the report calls it 'a second, independent axis'
note: mouse myocardial ischaemia-reperfusion and cardiomyocytes (not cancer); report counts it as separate support, but it is HDAC4 and no MEF2 is involved; title abbreviated in table

content: Class IIa HDACs repress MEF2 'in a deacetylase-independent manner' by sequestering it in an inactive form in the nucleus
note: table title 'Class II HDACs & ICP0 of HSV-1'

content: Vertebrate class IIa catalytic domains have only 'weak but measurable deacetylase activity', restorable by active-site His to Tyr mutation or non-acetylated lysine substrate
note: class-level, not HDAC5-specific; inversion at L24: class IIa carry His where other HDACs carry Tyr, the report writes the opposite ('histidine is naturally replaced by tyrosine')

content: A small molecule blocking the weak pocket targets a minor function while MEF2 sequestration and localization remain operational
Purified HDAC5 binds MEF2A directly; SPR gives nanomolar affinity (3.5-19.1 nM) across HDAC4/5/7/9 via conserved hydrophobic contacts
note: range is across class IIa, not HDAC5 alone

content: In hippocampal neurons spontaneous activity exported HDAC4 but not HDAC5; HDAC5 export followed NMDA-receptor or L-type calcium channel stimulation; more CaM-kinase-sensitive than HDAC4
note: cultured hippocampal neurones; the abstract names no species

content: HDAC5 repression is governed by catalysis-independent localization and localization control is paralog-specific
HDAC4 and HDAC5 repressed Bdnf promoter IV; class II inhibitor MC1568 rapidly derepressed it, though MEF2 element not required for that induction
note: MC1568 named in passing; inhibitor did derepress

content: Catalytic inhibitors act on only part of the class IIa repressive output
note: interpretation of a result in which the inhibitor was effective

content: Enzymatic activity relevant to repression is HDAC3's bridged by HDAC5 scaffold, so an HDAC5 catalytic inhibitor misses it
HDAC-PROTACs degrade HDACs via ubiquitin-proteasome, eliminating enzymatic and scaffolding functions; selective class IIa (e.g. HDAC4) degraders already exist
A selective HDAC7 PROTAC uncovered a deacetylase-independent function catalytic inhibitors could not reveal; current inhibitors are pan-inhibitory
HDAC7 PROTAC precedent is direct proof-of-principle that degradation and catalytic inhibition differ for class IIa scaffold biology
Selective class IIa/HDAC5 catalytic inhibitor (Arm 1); existing class IIa inhibitors largely pan-selective, truly HDAC5-selective inhibitors may not exist
Selective HDAC5 PROTAC degrader (Arm 2); HDAC5-selective degraders may not yet be optimized
MC1568 class II HDAC inhibitor (mentioned only inside Bdnf evidence)
HDAC5 (class IIa) as pharmacological target; HDAC4 paralog as comparator; HDAC3 as recruited enzyme; MEF2 and SLC2A1/GLUT1 as pathway nodes; HIF1alpha as Warburg node
Alternative routes if scaffold-dependent: selective HDAC5 degrader or a localization modulator (forced nuclear export), not a catalytic inhibitor

Decisive experiment in WWOX-deficient human neurons (patient iPSC-derived and/or isogenic WWOX-KO NPC-derived): inhibitor vs HDAC5 siRNA/shRNA and PROTAC vs structure-function rescue, HDAC4 comparator throughout
Rescue panel in knockdown background: WT HDAC5, catalytic-dead, MEF2-binding-deficient, 14-3-3 S to A nuclear-locked, cytoplasm-locked mutants
note: predicted outcomes table L73-81 is prediction not data

content: Molecular read-outs: SLC2A1 mRNA qPCR, GLUT1 protein, MEF2 reporter, HDAC5/MEF2 ChIP at SLC2A1 promoter, glucose uptake (2-NBDG or 3H-2-deoxyglucose)
Functional read-outs: ATP/ADP, lactate, Seahorse OCR vs ECAR, neuronal survival, multi-electrode-array network excitability/seizure-like activity
Paralog control: parallel HDAC4 knockdown/degrader; confirm HDAC5-selective degradation by Western across class IIa members
Preliminary: confirm HDAC5 to SLC2A1 axis directly in neurons via promoter ChIP and MEF2-reporter before committing to full 'ARMS' design
Characterize baseline GLUT1/glucose uptake in WWOX-deficient vs isogenic control neurons (is GLUT1 already elevated via HIF1alpha?)
Cross-check HIF1alpha dependence by combining HDAC5 perturbation with HIF1alpha knockdown to separate scaffold/MEF2 axis from Warburg axis
Decision rule: catalytic inhibition viable only if selective inhibitor reproduces degrader's GLUT1 rise and beneficial signature AND catalytic-dead mutant fails to restore repression
If catalytic-dead rescues and/or only degrader raises GLUT1: effect is scaffold/localization-dependent; use degrader or localization modulator
If raising GLUT1 worsens metabolic/excitability signature (OCR collapse, hyperexcitability): direction maladaptive; abandon manipulation regardless of mechanism
Direct SLC2A1 evidence is HDAC4-based (cardiac, cancer); HDAC5 evidence covers scaffold and localization only; no direct HDAC5 to SLC2A1 promoter demonstration in neurons
note: self-declared; neither cited paper is cancer: both are mouse cardiac HDAC4 (heart failure after infarction; ischaemia-reperfusion)
